raw_text:
Below is a progressive, 12‑week bodyweight strength program tailored for a 27‑year‑old male beginner training in a small flat with only a yoga mat and a doorway pull‑up bar. It’s focused on building full‑body strength, improving pull‑up ability, increasing push strength and leg strength, and establishing good movement patterns and recovery habits. Progression is built by increasing reps, sets, changing leverage/tempo, adding pauses, and increasing frequency/intensity. Sessions are short (30–50 min) and designed for minimal space.

Guidelines before you start
- Warm‑up (every session, 5–8 min): 1–2 min light cardio in place (marching knees, butt kicks, jumping jacks if space), dynamic mobility: arm circles, hip circles, leg swings, 10 bodyweight squats, 6–8 scapular pull‑ups or active hangs. Finish with movement‑specific activation (e.g., 8–10 bird dogs, 10 glute bridges).
- Cool‑down (5 min): light stretching (pecs, lats, hip flexors, quads, hamstrings), breathing work to return heart rate to baseline.
- Rest between sets: 60–120s for main strength sets; 30–60s for accessory/conditioning. Adjust depending on fatigue.
- Frequency: 4 sessions per week (recommended split: Upper/Lower/Upper/Lower). Two rest days (e.g., Wed & Sun) or active recovery days (walking, mobility).
- Form & tempo: Focus on controlled tempo. Typical tempo notation: eccentric/hold/concentric (e.g., 3/1/1 = 3s lowering, 1s pause, 1s up). Beginners often benefit from slower eccentrics to build strength.
- Progression strategies: increase reps/sets, decrease assistance, increase time under tension (slower eccentrics), add paused reps, reduce rest, add extra sets or an extra session of a weak movement each week.
- Pull‑up progression: important to build vertical pulling early. Use full active hang, scapular pull‑ups, negatives, assisted (feet on floor or chair) and eventually unassisted reps.
- Safety: watch for shoulder pain; back pain—keep neutral spine; stop if sharp pain occurs and refer to healthcare.

Weekly structure (example weekly schedule)
- Monday: Upper A (pull emphasis)
- Tuesday: Lower A
- Wednesday: Rest / mobility walk
- Thursday: Upper B (push emphasis)
- Friday: Lower B
- Sat: Optional light conditioning / mobility or rest
- Sun: Rest

Phases overview
- Weeks 1–4 (Foundation): Build movement quality, base strength, learn pull‑up progressions. Moderate volume, focus on form.
- Weeks 5–8 (Build): Increase load (reps/sets/tempo challenges), reduce assistance on pulls, add harder variations.
- Weeks 9–12 (Intensify & Test): Highest intensity, attempt strict unassisted pull‑ups, harder push/leg variations, test 1–3RM equivalents with bodyweight (max reps), taper last week for testing.

Detailed week‑by‑week plan
Notation: Sets x reps (tempo). If progression calls for RPE aim ~7–8 (challenging but doable). For AMRAPs do as many good reps as possible with strict form.

Weeks 1–4 — Foundation (4 sessions/week)
Goal: motor control, build pulling/pushing/leg base, introduce progressions.

Week 1
Upper A (Mon)
- Warm up
- Active hangs / scapular pull‑ups: 3 x 8–10s hangs or 8 scapular pulls (hang, pull shoulder blades down) (controlled)
- Incline push‑ups (hands on wall/door frame or table to reduce load) 4 x 8 (3/1/1)
- Negative pull‑ups (use step/chair to get chin above bar, then 3–4s descend) 4 x 3–5
- Pike rows (body angled, feet on floor, hands on doorway edge or bar) 3 x 8
- Plank: 3 x 30s

Lower A (Tue)
- Warm up
- Bodyweight squats: 4 x 10 (3/0/1)
- Reverse lunges (stationary): 3 x 8 each side
- Glute bridges (single leg progressions if easy): 3 x 10
- Nordics prep: Nordic lowering negatives with feet anchored under couch/door wedge if possible, otherwise slow hamstring slides on mat: 3 x 6 (eccentric focus)
- Side plank: 2 x 20–30s each side

Upper B (Thu)
- Warm up
- Assisted chin‑ups (feet on chair, knees bent) 4 x 6–8
- Knee or incline push‑ups 4 x 10
- Bodyweight rows under bar (horizontal rows; if bar low enough; otherwise do pike rows) 3 x 8–10
- Dumbbell replacement: Triceps dips on edge of sturdy chair (if safe) or close‑grip push‑ups on knees 3 x 8
- Dead bug: 3 x 8 each side

Lower B (Fri)
- Warm up
- Split squats (rear foot elevated if possible) 3 x 8 each leg
- Romanian single‑leg hip hinge (RDL motion without weight) 3 x 8 each leg
- Step‑ups to a chair/step 3 x 8 each side
- Calf raises (double then single-leg progression) 3 x 12
- Bird dog: 3 x 8 each side

Progressions for Weeks 2–4
- Week 2: Add 1 set to main exercises (e.g., squats 5 x 10), increase negative pull‑up duration to 4–5s, add 2–5 reps where possible.
- Week 3: Start incline push‑ups lower angle (hands on lower surface) and decrease assistance for chin/pull progressions (shorter reach for feet support). Replace some rows with bodyweight rows under the bar if possible. Add 1–2 seconds to eccentric of push/pull movements.
- Week 4: Introduce 1 set AMRAP of pull progression (attempt max assisted pull or negative count) and add paused reps (1–2s pause at bottom or mid). Aim to be able to do at least active hang + 5–8s and 2–3 assisted chin/pull reps with minimal assistance.

Weeks 5–8 — Build (4 sessions/week)
Goal: increase intensity and strength by reducing assistance, increasing time under tension, adding harder progressions.

General notes: Start aiming for 3–5 true (strict) chin‑ups/pull‑ups by end of week 8 if client responds well.

Week 5
Upper A (Mon)
- Warm up
- Active hang 3 x 10–15s
- Australian/body rows under bar (horizontal rows) 4 x 8–10 (slow 3/1/1)
- Assisted pull‑ups with feet lower (on ball of foot on chair) 4 x 5–6 (slow negatives on last rep)
- Elevated feet push‑ups (feet on low surface to increase difficulty) 4 x 8
- Hollow hold: 3 x 20s

Lower A (Tue)
- Warm up
- Deep slow squats (3–4s down) 5 x 8
- Bulgarian split squats (rear foot elevated) 3 x 8 each
- Glute bridge march (single‑leg emphasis) 3 x 10
- Nordic negatives (assisted) 3 x 6–8
- Plank with alternating leg lifts: 3 x 30–40s

Upper B (Thu)
- Warm up
- Pull progression: Negatives 4 x 4–6 (4–6s down), attempt 1–2 strict chin‑up attempts in warmup if able
- Archer or decline push‑up regressions: 4 x 6–8 each side (if too hard do close‑hand push‑ups)
- Body rows with elevated feet (increase angle) 4 x 8
- Triceps dips on edge (weighted by backpack if ready) or close‑grip elevated push‑ups: 3 x 8–10
- Side plank with reach under: 3 x 20s each side

Lower B (Fri)
- Warm up
- Pistol squat negatives to a chair (slow descent) 4 x 5 each leg (use support)
- Reverse lunges with tempo 4 x 8 each leg
- Single‑leg Romanian hip hinge 3 x 8
- Calf raises single‑leg 3 x 10–12
- Core: Russian twists 3 x 12 each side

Week 6–7 Progressions
- Reduce assistance on pull‑ups each week (lower foot support, fewer bands if using homemade assistance like a towel loop).
- Increase sets for rows/pushes to 5 if recovery allows.
- Add 1–2 reps per set or push 3–5s slower eccentrics.
- Add weighted challenge using backpack with books for squats, lunges, and elevated push‑ups only when technique is perfect.

Week 8 (end of phase)
- Test: Max strict chin‑up attempt (after warm‑up). Record best single set.
- If able to do 3–5 strict chin‑ups, begin adding rep sets of unassisted pulls next phase.
- Expect lower body exercises to be fairly challenging — aim for controlled single‑leg strength improvements.

Weeks 9–12 — Intensify & Test (4 sessions/week)
Goal: move toward unassisted pull‑ups, harder push and leg variants, max strength tests at end of week 12.

Structure changes
- Introduce more advanced variations: archer pull rows, uneven push‑ups (one hand elevated), full pistol progressions, slow eccentric singles for pull‑ups.
- Add one “test” session in Week 12 to assess 1RM equivalents: max strict pull‑ups (sets), max push‑ups in one set, max single‑leg squat reps to box.

Week 9
Upper A (Mon)
- Warm up
- Active hang + scap pulls: 3 x 15s
- Pulls: 5 sets of assisted pull‑ups with minimal assistance (use knee or single foot) 5 x 4–6 (try for last sets near failure)
- Bodyweight rows (close grip) 4 x 10 (slow)
- Decline push‑ups (feet elevated) 5 x 8–10
- Hollow body rocks: 3 x 30s

Lower A (Tue)
- Warm up
- Pistol progressions to box: 5 x 5 each side (slow negatives)
- Walking lunges or stationary lunges with added tempo: 4 x 10 each
- Single‑leg glute bridge weighted progressions (backpack) 4 x 8 each
- Nordic negatives 4 x 6–8
- Plank variations 3 x 45s

Week 10
Upper B (Thu)
- Warm up
- Attempt sets of strict chin/pull: 6 sets of 2–4 strict reps (if you can do 1–2 reps, do more sets across the day) — emphasis quality
- One‑arm‑assist push‑ups (one hand on towel or elevated) 4 x 6 each side or slow close‑grip push‑ups 4 x 8
- Archer body rows / staggered rows under bar 4 x 6 each side
- Triceps negative dips (use chair) 3 x 6–8
- Core: L‑holds or tucked L‑holds 3 x 20s

Lower B (Fri)
- Warm up
- Box pistol or full pistol attempts: 5 x 4–6 each leg
- Bulgarian split squats with slow tempo: 4 x 8
- Single‑leg RDL to balance: 4 x 8 each
- Calf work: 4 x 12 single‑leg
- Side planks 3 x 40s each

Week 11
- Similar to week 9–10 but aim to increase intensity: shorten rest, increase eccentrics to 5–6s on negatives, add one AMRAP set for push‑ups or rows.
- If client can do 3–5 strict pull‑ups, start programming 3–5 sets of 3–5 strict reps. Otherwise continue negatives and assisted sets.

Week 12 — Test & Deload
Upper A (Mon) — Test day 1
- Warm up well
- Max strict chin‑ups: perform 3 attempts separated by 2–3 min; record max reps (best single set).
- 3 x max strict push‑ups (one set to failure) for baseline.
- Short accessory: 3 x 8 body rows, 3 x plank 45s

Lower (Tue) — Test day 2
- Warm up
- Max unbroken single‑leg squat to box reps each side (or max bodyweight squats for reps) — record.
- Max unbroken bodyweight split squats (each leg) or timed AMRAP 3 min of lunges.
- Short accessory core work.

Thu (Deload)
- Light full‑body session: 2 sets of all movements at 50% volume and no max efforts:
  - 2 x 6 assisted pull/chin progressions
  - 2 x 8 incline push‑ups
  - 2 x 8 slow squats
  - Mobility & extended stretching

Fri or Sat — Reassess goals and advise next steps: maintenance, continued progression to more advanced bodyweight skills, or add external load (backpack) if available.

Accessory & conditioning additions (optional)
- Conditioning (once/week optional): 10–15 min circuit (jumping jacks, mountain climbers, high knees, bodyweight squats) 30–40s work / 20s rest x 6 rounds. Keep separate from strength days or after accessory work.
- Grip strength: passive hangs 3 x 20–30s, towel hangs if grip is strong enough.

Nutrition & recovery guidance
- Protein: Aim for ~1.6–2.0 g/kg bodyweight per day to support strength gains (e.g., 75–100 g/day for a 47–62 kg athlete; adjust to client weight). If client weighs more, scale accordingly. Spread protein across meals.
- Calories: For beginner wanting strength and to gain lean mass, aim for a small calorie surplus (~+200–300 kcal/day) if weight gain is acceptable. If wanting to maintain weight while getting stronger, eat at maintenance and prioritize protein.
- Hydration: 2–3 L/day baseline, more around workouts.
- Sleep: 7–9 hours nightly recommended—sleep is critical for strength gains.
- Recovery: Active recovery (walking, mobility), foam rolling if available. If sore, reduce volume next session or take extra rest day.
- Post‑workout: simple carb + protein snack within 1–2 hours can help recovery (e.g., sandwich, yogurt & fruit).

Notes on progression and troubleshooting
- If progress stalls on pull‑ups: increase frequency of specific pull practice (add 2 short sessions a week of 3–5 sets of assisted pulls/negatives), add more rows and scapular work, and do weighted backpack negatives gradually.
- If push‑ups plateau: change leverage (decline for harder, incline for easier), use slow eccentrics, add paused reps at bottom.
- If legs are lagging: emphasize single‑leg work and increase volume gradually; use backpack for progressive overload.
- Keep a training log: record sets, reps, perceived exertion, and any issues. This helps adjust load and progression.

Sample microprogression for pull‑ups across 12 weeks (example)
- Weeks 1–2: active hangs, scap pulls, 3–5s negatives, assisted chin‑ups 4–6 reps × 3–4 sets
- Weeks 3–5: reduce assistance, increase negative time to 5s, body rows 3–5 sets
- Weeks 6–8: try 1–3 strict reps, increase sets of strict reps, continue negatives
- Weeks 9–12: aim for multiple sets of strict reps (3–5 sets of 2–5 reps), test max in week 12

Final notes
- Emphasize perfect technique over chasing reps. For a beginner, consistent practice beats sporadic high intensity.
- Adjust volume if client’s recovery is poor (reduce a set or reduce intensity).
- If any joint pain appears (especially shoulders or knees), regress the movement and refer as needed.

If you want, I can:
- Customize rep counts and progression to his exact bodyweight and baseline testing results.
- Make a printable week‑by‑week schedule (calendar view).
- Provide a 7‑day sample meal plan to match goals (surplus/maintenance/cut).
